source.name: tr_OrderAudit
source.sourceDefinition:
CREATE   TRIGGER dbo.tr_OrderAudit
ON dbo.Orders
AFTER INSERT
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    INSERT INTO dbo.OrderMetadata (OrderID, MetadataXml)
    SELECT i.OrderID, CAST('<audit><timestamp>' + CONVERT(VARCHAR(30), GETDATE(), 126) + '</timestamp></audit>' AS XML)
    FROM inserted i
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dbo.OrderMetadata m WHERE m.OrderID = i.OrderID);
END;

result.generatedDdl:
-- Trigger function for OrderAudit
CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION dbo.tr_OrderAudit_func()
RETURNS TRIGGER AS $$
BEGIN
    -- Insert audit metadata for new orders that don't already have metadata
    INSERT INTO dbo.OrderMetadata (OrderID, MetadataXml)
    SELECT i.OrderID, 
           XMLPARSE(DOCUMENT '<audit><timestamp>' || TO_CHAR(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS') || '</timestamp></audit>')
    FROM new_table i
    WHERE NOT EXISTS (
        SELECT 1 
        FROM dbo.OrderMetadata m 
        WHERE m.OrderID = i.OrderID
    );
    
    RETURN NULL; -- AFTER trigger on statement level
END;
$$ LANGUAGE plpgsql;

-- Create the trigger
CREATE TRIGGER tr_OrderAudit
AFTER INSERT ON dbo.Orders
REFERENCING NEW TABLE AS new_table
FOR EACH STATEMENT
EXECUTE FUNCTION dbo.tr_OrderAudit_func();
assumptions: The dbo schema exists in PostgreSQL or will be created
The OrderMetadata table exists with columns OrderID and MetadataXml of type XML
The Orders table has an OrderID column
XML data type is available in PostgreSQL (requires XML support to be enabled)
Statement-level trigger is appropriate since the original trigger processes the inserted set as a whole
ISO 8601 timestamp format (YYYY-MM-DDTHH24:MI:SS) is acceptable replacement for SQL Server style 126 format
CURRENT_TIMESTAMP provides equivalent functionality to GETDATE()

reviewFlags.reason: XML construction and timestamp formatting differs from SQL Server. Verify the exact timestamp format requirements and XML structure match business needs. SQL Server CONVERT style 126 produces 'YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MI:SS.mmm' format with milliseconds.
Verify that the NOT EXISTS logic correctly handles concurrent inserts. PostgreSQL's MVCC may behave differently than SQL Server in high-concurrency scenarios.
Statement-level triggers with transition tables require PostgreSQL 10+. Verify PostgreSQL version compatibility.

compatibilityNotes.description: SQL Server CONVERT(VARCHAR(30), GETDATE(), 126) produces ISO 8601 format with milliseconds (e.g., '2024-01-15T10:30:45.123'). PostgreSQL TO_CHAR with 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS' omits milliseconds. Add '.MS' to format string if milliseconds are required.
SQL Server uses CAST to XML, PostgreSQL uses XMLPARSE(DOCUMENT ...). Both create XML data types but parsing behavior may differ for malformed XML.
Both SQL Server and PostgreSQL execute this as a statement-level trigger (once per INSERT statement), but PostgreSQL requires explicit REFERENCING clause for transition tables.
PostgreSQL does not have an equivalent to SET NOCOUNT ON. This is not needed in PostgreSQL as triggers don't return row counts to the client by default.
PostgreSQL triggers execute within the same transaction as the triggering statement. If the trigger fails, the entire operation rolls back, consistent with SQL Server behavior.
